name: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

terms.definition: The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
terms.examiner: The atomic (proton) number is the number of protons in the nucleus.

terms.definition: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
terms.examiner: Isotopes of an element have the same electronic configuration, so the same chemical properties.

terms.definition: The mass of an atom of an isotope, relative to one-twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
terms.examiner: It refers to one isotope; relative atomic mass is the weighted mean for the element.

terms.definition: The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element, relative to one-twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
terms.examiner: "Weighted mean" and the carbon-12 comparison are both needed. From a mass spectrum, multiply each isotopic mass by its abundance, add, and divide by the total abundance.

terms.definition: A region within an atom that can hold up to two electrons with opposite spins.
terms.examiner: An s sub-shell has one orbital, p has three and d has five.

terms.definition: The energy required to remove an electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms.
terms.examiner: "Gaseous" is needed, and the equation must have state symbols: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

terms.definition: A repeating pattern in properties across different periods of the Periodic Table.
terms.examiner: Be ready to explain the trends in ionisation energy and melting temperature across Periods 2 and 3.
